title: Daskam 39 — Yogamaya and Krishna’s Birth in Gokula
description: The Yamuna crossing, Yogamaya’s manifestation and warning, Krishna’s birth celebration in Gokula, and Nanda’s auspicious rites.

source.translation_note: No sourced English translation is included; meaning_en fields are clearly marked editorial drafts.

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवन्तमयमुद्वहन् यदुकुलोद्वहो निस्सरन्
ददर्श गगनोच्चलज्जलभरां कलिन्दात्मजाम् ।
अहो सलिलसञ्चयः स पुनरैन्द्रजालोदितो
जलौघ इव तत् क्षणात् प्रपदमेयतामाययौ ॥ ३९-१ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Vasudeva carries the infant Krishna from Mathura and sees the Yamuna’s flood fall to ankle depth.
stanzas.commentary_en: When Vasudeva set out carrying Baby Krishna, he saw the waters of the Yamuna river flooded to the skies.  As he crossed, the waters were reduced to the ankles of his feet as if it was an illusory flood caused by magic.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavantamayamudvahan yadukulodvaho nissaran
dadarśa gaganoccalajjalabharāṃ kalindātmajām |
aho salilasañcayaḥ sa punaraindrajālodito
jalaugha iva tat kṣaṇāt prapadameyatāmāyayau || 39-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रसुप्तपशुपालिकां निभृतमारुदद्बालिका-
-मपावृतकवाटिकां पशुपवाटिकामाविशन् ।
भवन्तमयमर्पयन् प्रसवतल्पके तत्पदा-
-द्वहन् कपटकन्यकां स्वपुरमागतो वेगतः ॥ ३९-२ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: At Nanda’s house, the sleeping village and opened doors allow Vasudeva to exchange the two newborns and return with the girl.
stanzas.commentary_en: At Gokulam, everyone were fast asleep. Doors of Nandagopan's house opened and the Yogamaya gave a shrill cry as if to announce the location of the house. Vasudeva left  baby Krishna near sleeping Yashoda and carried the girl child to reach Mathura faster.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prasuptapaśupālikāṃ nibhṛtamārudadbālikā-
-mapāvṛtakavāṭikāṃ paśupavāṭikāmāviśan |
bhavantamayamarpayan prasavatalpake tatpadā-
-dvahan kapaṭakanyakāṃ svapuramāgato vegataḥ || 39-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततस्त्वदनुजारवक्षपितनिद्रवेगद्रव-
-द्भटोत्करनिवेदितप्रसववार्तयैवार्तिमान् ।
विमुक्तचिकुरोत्करस्त्वरितमापतन् भोजरा-
-डतुष्ट इव दृष्टवान् भगिनिकाकरे कन्यकाम् ॥ ३९-३ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Kamsa rushes to the prison after the newborn girl’s cry and sees her in Devaki’s arms.
stanzas.commentary_en: After reaching the prison,  the child’s (Yogamaya) crying sound made the guards rush to inform Kamsa that the 8th baby is born. Kamsa came running in anger and agitation to the prison cell, but was confused to see a baby girl in his sister Devaki's hands.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tatastvadanujāravakṣapitanidravegadrava-
-dbhaṭotkaraniveditaprasavavārtayaivārtimān |
vimuktacikurotkarastvaritamāpatan bhojarā-
-ḍatuṣṭa iva dṛṣṭavān bhaginikākare kanyakām || 39-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ध्रुवं कपटशालिनो मधुहरस्य माया भवे-
-दसाविति किशोरिकां भगिनिकाकरालिङ्गिताम् ।
द्विपो नलिनिकान्तरादिव मृणालिकामाक्षिप-
-न्नयं त्वदनुजामजामुपलपट्टके पिष्टवान् ॥ ३९-४ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Believing the girl is a divine trick, Kamsa seizes her and prepares to dash her against a stone; the scene is shown before any impact.
stanzas.commentary_en: Kamsa thought to himself that this must be some maaya of Lord Vishnu. He snatched the baby from Devaki's hands like an elephant snatching and plucking the lotus from the pond and lifted his hand to hit it hard on the stone slab.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dhruvaṃ kapaṭaśālino madhuharasya māyā bhave-
-dasāviti kiśorikāṃ bhaginikākarāliṅgitām |
dvipo nalinikāntarādiva mṛṇālikāmākṣipa-
-nnayaṃ tvadanujāmajāmupalapaṭṭake piṣṭavān || 39-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततो भवदुपासको झटिति मृत्युपाशादिव
प्रमुच्य तरसैव सा समधिरूढरूपान्तरा ।
अधस्तलमजग्मुषी विकसदष्टबाहुस्फुर-
-न्महायुधमहो गता किल विहायसा दिद्युते ॥ ३९-५ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Freed from Kamsa, Yogamaya assumes her radiant eight-armed goddess form above the ground.
stanzas.commentary_en: The baby child, Yoga Maayaa freed herself from the clutches of Kamsa immediately. Not hitting the earth, she rose above the earth in the sky and took a divine form with powerful weapons in her eight arms.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tato bhavadupāsako jhaṭiti mṛtyupāśādiva
pramucya tarasaiva sā samadhirūḍharūpāntarā |
adhastalamajagmuṣī vikasadaṣṭabāhusphura-
-nmahāyudhamaho gatā kila vihāyasā didyute || 39-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
नृशंसतर कंस ते किमु मया विनिष्पिष्टया
बभूव भवदन्तकः क्वचन चिन्त्यतां ते हितम् ।
इति त्वदनुजा विभो खलमुदीर्य तं जग्मुषी
मरुद्गणपणायिता भुवि च मन्दिराण्येयुषी ॥ ३९-६ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Yogamaya warns Kamsa that his destined slayer was born elsewhere, then departs as devas honor her.
stanzas.commentary_en: Yogamaya called out to the cruel king Kamsa and said that there is no use in killing her, the person who is going to kill him is born elsewhere.  Yogamaaya then vanished in to the different temples in the earth while devas sprinkled flowers on her.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nṛśaṃsatara kaṃsa te kimu mayā viniṣpiṣṭayā
babhūva bhavadantakaḥ kvacana cintyatāṃ te hitam |
iti tvadanujā vibho khalamudīrya taṃ jagmuṣī
marudgaṇapaṇāyitā bhuvi ca mandirāṇyeyuṣī || 39-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रगे पुनरगात्मजावचनमीरिता भूभुजा
प्रलम्बबकपूतनाप्रमुखदानवा मानिनः ।
भवन्निधनकाम्यया जगति बभ्रमुर्निर्भयाः
कुमारकविमारकाः किमिव दुष्करं निष्कृपैः ॥ ३९-७ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Kamsa addresses the asura leaders; their departure is represented without depicting harm to infants.
stanzas.commentary_en:
Kamsa informed his demons Pralamba, Baka, and Poothana about Yogamaya's words. The asuras went around  killing all the male infants all around the world.
Merciless people are capable of doing merciless deeds.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prage punaragātmajāvacanamīritā bhūbhujā
pralambabakapūtanāpramukhadānavā māninaḥ |
bhavannidhanakāmyayā jagati babhramurnirbhayāḥ
kumārakavimārakāḥ kimiva duṣkaraṃ niṣkṛpaiḥ || 39-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततः पशुपमन्दिरे त्वयि मुकुन्द नन्दप्रिया-
-प्रसूतिशयनेशये रुदति किञ्चिदञ्चत्पदे ।
विबुध्य वनिताजनैस्तनयसम्भवे घोषिते
मुदा किमु वदाम्यहो सकलमाकुलं गोकुलम् ॥ ३९-८ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Krishna’s birth wakes Gokula, where Yashoda, Nanda, and the cowherd women celebrate.
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan baby Krishna now gave a cry announcing his birth in Gokulam, waking up Yashoda. She immediately informed Nandagopan and all gopikas, the happy news of arrival of male child. The whole Gokula rejoiced the arrival of the child.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tataḥ paśupamandire tvayi mukunda nandapriyā-
-prasūtiśayaneśaye rudati kiñcidañcatpade |
vibudhya vanitājanaistanayasambhave ghoṣite
mudā kimu vadāmyaho sakalamākulaṃ gokulam || 39-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अहो खलु यशोदया नवकलायचेतोहरं
भवन्तमलमन्तिके प्रथममापिबन्त्या दृशा ।
पुनः स्तनभरं निजं सपदि पाययन्त्या मुदा
मनोहरतनुस्पृशा जगति पुण्यवन्तो जिताः ॥ ३९-९ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Yashoda gazes lovingly at Krishna and feeds him.
stanzas.commentary_en: Yasodha looked at baby Krishna who was as fresh as the kaayambu flower, fed him with milk, touched and caressed him and felt extremely happy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aho khalu yaśodayā navakalāyacetoharaṃ
bhavantamalamantike prathamamāpibantyā dṛśā |
punaḥ stanabharaṃ nijaṃ sapadi pāyayantyā mudā
manoharatanuspṛśā jagati puṇyavanto jitāḥ || 39-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवत्कुशलकाम्यया स खलु नन्दगोपस्तदा
प्रमोदभरसङ्कुलो द्विजकुलाय किं नाददात् ।
तथैव पशुपालकाः किमु न मङ्गलं तेनिरे
जगत्त्रयमङ्गल त्वमिह पाहि मामामयात् ॥ ३९-१० ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Nanda gives gifts to Brahmins and the cowherds perform auspicious rites; the closing prayer is carried by the devotional composition, without placing Bhattathiri in the historical scene.
stanzas.commentary_en:
Nandagopa, overwhelmed with joy distributed gifts to all holy Brahmins and performed all rituals for baby's welfare.

Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan who blesses auspiciousness to all in the three worlds to ward off his diseases and protect him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavatkuśalakāmyayā sa khalu nandagopastadā
pramodabharasaṅkulo dvijakulāya kiṃ nādadāt |
tathaiva paśupālakāḥ kimu na maṅgalaṃ tenire
jagattrayamaṅgala tvamiha pāhi māmāmayāt || 39-10 ||
